SPECIFICATION FOR STEEL TUBES FOR HEAT EXCHANGERS
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Parts 1 to 5 ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 5 May 1986, after the draft finalized by the Steel Tubes, Pipes and Fittings Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council. 0.2 Welded and seamless carbon and alloy steel tubes are extensively used in heat transfer equipment, such as tubular heat exchangers and condensers. This standard is intended to cover their quality requircmcnts. 0.3 This standard keeps in view the manufacturing and trade practices followed in the country as well as by reputed international tube manufacturers in this field. In the preparation of this standard due consideration has been given to the need for international co-ordination among standards being followed in other countries and assistance has been derived from the following publications: ASTM A 179.1983 Seamless cold finished and condenser tubes. ASTM A 213-1983 boiler, superheater drawn low carbon steel alloy hot steel

Seamless ferritic and austenitic and heat exchanger tubes. steel boiler,

ASTM A 249-1983 Welded austenitic heat exchanger and condenser tubes. ASME Section for carbon, IS0 II SA 450 Specification ferritic alloys and austenitic

superheater,

for general requirements alloy steel tubes. exchangers. Interna-

6758-1980 Welded steel tubes for heat tional Organization for Standardization.

0.4 To facilitate additions and alterations to the standard and to provide convenience to the users of the standard, the standard is being publis~tl into 5 parts, but in one volume, a? given below: Part 1 General Seamless carbon steel tubes 3

PART 1 GENERAL

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 1 ) covers welded and seamless carbon and steel tubes for tubular heat exchangers, condensers and other similar transfer equipments. 2. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

iS : 11714 ( Part 1 ) - 1986 4. MANUFACTURE 4. I Tubes shall be made by automatic welding process or scamless or shall be either hot finished or cold drawn, as specified. process

4.2 For welded tubes, the tubes shall bc made from flat-rolled steel by an automatic welding process with no addrtion of filler metal. Seamless tubes may be supplied either in hot finished or cold drawn condition at the manufacturer's option, unless otherwise specified by the purchaser. Cold drawn tubes shall be suitably heat-treated. 5. SURFACE CONDITION AND FINISH

5.1 Finished tubes shall be clean internally and externally, and free from scale. Ends shall be plain, frrc from burrs and square cut with the axis of the tube. ( A slight amount of oxidation will not bc considered as scale. ) 5.2 Tubes shall be reasonably straight, smooth and cylindrical.

5.3 Surface marks may be dressed smooth by grinding provided the thickncss of the tube after dressing is not less than the required minimum thickness. The drcsscd area shall blcntl iuto the contour of the tube. 5.4 If Lhc ends of` tubes arc subjected to cold working conditions heat-treatment, then the ends ( 3_YJmm long ) shall be suitably treated. 5.5 Stainless steel tubes shall be pickled free from bright annealing is used, pickling is not necessary. 6. TESTS 6.1 Tensile Properties as to tensile properties scale, ho\zcver after heat when

6.2 The material shall conform to the requirements prescribed in the individual specification.

6.3 The yield point shall be dctcrmined by the drop of the pointer, by the halt in the gauge pointer of the testing machine, or by other approved methods. When definite yield strength is not exhibited, the yield strength corresponding to a permanent off set of 0.2 percent of the gauge length of the s@ecimen, or to a total extension of 0.5 percent of the gauge length under load, shall be determined. 7. 13. NON-DESTRUCTIVE

ELECTRIC

TEST

13.1 Each tube shall be tested with a non-destructive electric test in accordance with methods given in IS : 6394-1971*, IS : 6398-19831_ and IS : 7343-1974f. It is the intent of this test to reject tubes containing injurious defects.
13.2 The following specification. information is for the benefit of the user of this

13.2.1 The ultrasonic examination referred in this specification is intended to detect longitudinal discontinuities having a reflective area similar to or larger than the calibration reference notches specified in 13.3. The examination may not detect circumferentially oriented imperfections or short, deep defects.
*Code of pr.lctice tCode of practict: $Code of practice for ultrasonic tpsting of seamless pipes and tubular for eddy cllrrent testing of seamless ferrous pipes for ultrasonic testing of welded pipes and tubular products. and tubes products. (Jir~!

reuision).

IO

IS : 11714( Part 1 ) - 1986 13.2.2 The eddy cm-rent examination referred to in this specification has the capability of detecting significant cliscontin\Gties, especially oF the short abrupt type. 13.2.3 The flux leakage examination referred to in this specification is capable of detecting the presence and location of significant longitudinally or transversely oriented discontinuities. It should be recognized that different techniques should be employed to detect differently oriented imperfections. 13.2.4 The hydrostatic test referred to in many product specifications. This test defects of a size permitting the test fluid to may be either visually seen or detected by defect or defects that extend an appreciable complete penetration.
is a test method provided for has the capability of finding leak through the tube wall and a loss of fluid through-the-wall distance into the wall without

13.2.5 A purchaser interested in ascertaining the nature ( type, size, location, and orientation ) or discontinuities that can be detected in the specific application of those examinations should discuss this with the manufacturer of the tubular product. 13.3 For eddy current testing, the calibration tube shall contain, at the option of the producer, any one of the following discontinuities to establish a minimum sensitivity level for rejection. For welded tubing they shall be placed in the weld, if visible. 13.3.1 Drilled Hole - A hole not larger than OS79 mm diameter shall be drilled radially and completely through the tube wall, care being taken to avoid distortion of the tubing while drilling, 13.3.2 Transverse Tangential Notch - Usin! a round tool or file with a 6.4 mm diameter, a notch shall be filed or mdled tangential to the surface and transverse to the longitudinal axis of the tube. The notch shall have a depth not exceeding 12.5 percent of the specified wall thickness of the tube or 0,102 mm whichever is greater. 13.3.3 Longitudinal Notch - A notch O-8 mm or less in width shall be machined in a radial plane parallel to the tube axis on the outside surface of the tube, to have a depth not cxcccding 12 -5 percent ofthe specified wall thickness of the tube or 0.102 mm, whichever is grcat.er. The length of the notch shall be compatible with the testing method.

13.4 For ultrasonic testing, the longitudinal calibration reference notches shall be at the option of the producer, any one of the three common notch `I'he shapes shown in and according to IS : (;3'34-1971* or IS : 7343-1'J7slf. depth of notch shall not cxcccc1 12.5 percent of the specified wall thickness of the tube or 0.102 mm whichever is greater. For welded tubing the notch shall be placed in the wclcl, if visible.
13.5 For flux leakage testing, the longitudinal calibration reference notches shall bc straight-sided notches machined in a radial plane parallel to the tube axis on the inside and outside surface of the tube. Notch depth shall not exceed 12.5 percent of the specified wall thickness, or 0,102 mm, whichever is greater. Notch length shall not exceed the depth. Outside diameter and inside diameter notches shall be located sufftcicntly apart to allow separation and identification of the signals. 13.6 Tubing producing a siFna1 equal to or greater than the calibration defect shall be subject to rejection. The area producing the signal may be examined. 13.6.1 Test signals produced by imperfections which cannot bc identified or produced by cracks or crack-like defects shall result in rejection of the tube subject to rework and retest. To be acceptrd, the tube should pass the same sI>ccilication test to which it was originally subjected provirlt~l that the tlimerisional requirements are met. 33.6.2 Test signals produced by imperfections such as those listed below may be jutI+ as in.juriour or non-injurious drpcnding on visual observation of their severity or the type of signal they produce on the testing equipment used, or both: a) Dingcs, b) Straightener marks, c) Loose ID bead and cutting d) Scratches, e) f) Steel die stamps, flash trim, or ripple. mm or 12.5 ) in depth Chattered chips,

14.1 Test specimens shall be taken from the ends of finished tubes prior expanding, or other forming operations, or being to upsetting, swaging, cut to length. `They shall be smooth on the ends and free from burrs and flaws. 14.2 If any test specimen shows flaws or defective discarded and another specimen substituted. 15. REPAIR BY WELDING machining, it may be

15.1 Repair welding of base metal dcfccts in tubing is permissible only with the approval ol` the purchaser and wit11 the further understanding that the tube shall be marked `WR' and the composition of the deposited filler metal shall be suitable for the composition being welded. Defects shall be thoroughly chipped or ground out before weldmg and each repaired length shall be reheat-trcatcd or stress rclicvcd as required by the applical)le specification. Each length of repaired tubes shall be tested hydrostatically as required by the product specification. 15.2 Repair welding procedures approved 16. RETESTS 16.1 If the results of the mechanical tests of any group or lot do not conform to the requirements specified in the individual specification, retests may bc made on additional tubes of double the original number from the same group or lot, each of which shall conform to the requirements specified. 17. 26.1.1 For use in certain corrosives, particularly chlorides where stress07Cr19Ni9Mo2. 04Cr corrosion may occur, tubes in grades 2OCr18Ni2, 19Ni9,04Cr19Ni9Nb40 and TP348* may be specified in the stress-relieved annealed condition. Cooling from this temperature range may be either in air or by slow cooling. No mechanical straightening is permitted after the stress-relief treatment. 26.1.3 Straightness of the tubes shall be a matter of agreement.

26.2 Air Underwater Pressure Test - Each tube, with internal surface clean and dry, shall be internally pressurized to 1 034 kPa minimum with clean and dry compressed air while being submerged in clean water. The tube shall bc well-lighted, preferably by underwater illumination. Inspection shall be made of the entire external surface ol' the tube after holding the pressure for not less than 5 seconds after the surface or the water has If any tube shows leakage during the air underwater test it become calm. shall be rejected. Any leaking areas may be cut and the tube retested.
